newsitem.title: CHINA: China to ease restrictions on foreign travel.
newsitem.headline: China to ease restrictions on foreign travel.

text.p: China will ease restrictions on foreign travel by its citizens by the end of 1996, official media said on Wednesday.
The move would simplify procedures for exit visas, make conditions for approval uniform and standardise fees nationwide, the China Daily and other major newspapers said.
A time limit for approval would also be set and people applying for personal passports would not be required to submit supporting documents other than those relevant for travelling, the reports said.

Passports would be valid for five years and no official would have the right to arbitrarily shorten the period, Xu Ganlu, director of the Bureau of Entry and Exit Administration under the Ministry of Public Security, was quoted as saying.
China eased restrictions on foreign travel in 1986, but regulations remain vague, and abuse of power by officials controlling access to passports and exit visas is a common complaint.
So far, only a tiny fraction of the population -- mostly the rich and powerful -- have been able to travel abroad.

Between January 1990 and June 1996, China allowed 4.3 million people to travel abroad for personal reasons, the China Daily said. Another 4.6 million visited Hong Kong and Macau and 140,000 others went to Taiwan.

In the first six months of 1996, 710,000 personal passports were issued, compared with 970,000 for the whole of 1995, the newspaper said. The number of personal passports issued in 1995 rose 37.5 percent from 1994.
